2: // The callback style is the point: Chapter 5 migrates the service layer off it.
3: 
4: const tables = {
5:   users: [

7:     { id: 2, email: 'grace@example.com', name: 'Grace', deleted_at: null },
8:     { id: 3, email: 'alan@example.com', name: 'Alan', deleted_at: '2026-01-04' },
9:   ],
10:   orders: [
11:     { id: 10, user_id: 1, total_cents: 4200, status: 'paid', deleted_at: null },
12:     { id: 11, user_id: 1, total_cents: 1350, status: 'quote', deleted_at: null },
13:     { id: 12, user_id: 2, total_cents: 9900, status: 'paid', deleted_at: null },
14:     { id: 13, user_id: 3, total_cents: 500, status: 'paid', deleted_at: null },
15:   ],
16:   payments: [
17:     { id: 100, order_id: 10, amount_cents: 4200, captured: true },
18:     { id: 101, order_id: 12, amount_cents: 9900, captured: false },
19:   ],
20: };
21: 
22: export function reset() {
23:   tables.users[2].deleted_at = '2026-01-04';
24:   tables.orders.forEach((o) => { o.deleted_at = null; });
25: }
26: 
27: // Old-style callback query. Accepts a table name and a predicate.
28: export function query(table, predicate, callback) {
29:   setImmediate(() => {
30:     const rows = tables[table];
31:     if (!rows) return callback(new Error(`no such table: ${table}`));
32:     try {
33:       callback(null, rows.filter(predicate).map((r) => ({ ...r })));
34:     } catch (err) {
35:       callback(err);
36:     }
37:   });
38: }
39: 
40: export function update(table, id, patch, callback) {
41:   setImmediate(() => {
42:     const row = (tables[table] || []).find((r) => r.id === id);
43:     if (!row) return callback(new Error(`no row ${id} in ${table}`));
44:     Object.assign(row, patch);
45:     callback(null, { ...row });
46:   });
47: }
